name: mature saskatoon serviceberry shrub
description: a tall, many-stemmed shrub with gray, shallowly furrowed bark

seasonDescription.spring: , oval leaves with rounded tips, and crowded clusters of white flowers
seasonDescription.summer: and oval leaves with rounded tips
seasonDescription.fall: and oval leaves in shades of yellow, orange, and red

details: A tall shrub grows here, nearly a small tree, its oldest stems as thick as a wrist and its suckers spread into a broad thicket.  The gray bark is shallowly furrowed on the old wood and still smooth and striped on the young stems.

seasonDetails.winter: The reddish-brown twigs end in narrow, pointed buds sheathed in several overlapping scales.  A few of the oldest stems have died back and stand gray and bare among the living ones.
seasonDetails.spring: The young leaves are oval to nearly round with blunt tips, coarsely toothed above the middle and smooth-edged below, and faintly downy beneath.  Short, crowded racemes of fragrant white flowers cover the whole thicket, each bloom carrying five narrow petals, and the shrub hums with bees.
seasonDetails.summer: The leaves are oval to nearly round, dull blue-green above and paler beneath, coarsely toothed along the upper half of each margin.
seasonDetails.fall: The leaves have turned to yellow, orange, and red.  They are oval to nearly round, coarsely toothed along the upper half of each margin.

keywords: mature saskatoon serviceberry juneberry shrub bush thicket gray furrowed bark oval leaves rounded tips stems tree

Harvestable.preDescription: The stems are bowed under clusters of dark purple berries, each dusted with a pale waxy bloom.
Harvestable.postDescription: The shrub has been picked clean of berries.
